faqs.question: Does Epson make drivers for Linux?
faqs.answer:
Linux drivers are available for some products. Visit the links below to see the drivers available for your product, as well as information about using an Epson product with Linux.
Note:
Epson does not provide support for Linux drivers.
Linux drivers for Epson products
Linux FAQs for Epson products
(only available in English)
Linux manuals for Epson products
(only available in English)

faqs.question: I am unable to connect my product to a wireless network. What should I do?
faqs.answer: The printer does not come with built-in wireless features and does not support a wireless (or Ethernet) connection to a network router. Only a direct wired connection to the computer is supported.

faqs.question: Can the Epson ink cartridges be refilled or can I use third-party ink cartridges without voiding the warranty?
faqs.answer:
Epson does not recommend refilling or using other brands of ink cartridges.  Epson uses a permanent Micro Piezo print head that has allowed Epson to lead the industry in delivering consistent photo image quality by using variable-sized droplets.  Micro Piezo print head can also use a wider variety of inks, which has allowed Epson to introduce such ink breakthroughs as DURABrite® and Epson UltraChrome® inks that offer greatly improved humidity resistance, smudge resistance, and fade resistance.
Using refilled ink cartridges will not void the product's original warranty; however, if these products cause a failure, the repair of that failure will not be covered under warranty.

faqs.question: When I try to print to my product in Windows 7, printing is slow or my product stops printing. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following:
Select a lower quality setting in the printer software.
Make sure your system meets the minimum system requirements for your printer.
Close the
Devices and Printers
window before you print.
Clear space on your hard drive or run a defragmentation utility.
Close programs that you're not using.
Increase your system's memory.

faqs.question: Heavy coated or thick paper does not load correctly or loads skewed. What should I do?
faqs.answer: The paper you are using may be too heavy or glossy for the paper roller to pick up. Be sure the paper is within printer specifications.

faqs.question: How do I obtain the latest product software for Windows or my Mac?
faqs.answer: You can download the latest product driver from the Downloads section of this website.

faqs.question: Can the printer still print if an ink cartridge is expended or not installed?
faqs.answer: No. The printer will not operate if any cartridge is expended or removed. It's best to always have extra cartridges on hand.

faqs.question: How do I change the font size of text when I print from software in Windows?
faqs.answer: You need to select the text or font size in the software you are printing from, not the printer driver. For detailed instructions, contact the company for the application you are printing from.

faqs.question: I brought my product with me to a different country and can't find ink for it. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Some Epson printers and ink cartridges are specific to a regional market and not sold worldwide, although the same printers are sold in the U.S. and Canada. If you have a printer sold in the U.S. or Canada, you may not be able to easily get ink cartridges for it in foreign markets.
Unfortunately, because of customs and tax regulations, the Epson E-Stores in the U.S. and Canada are unable to ship to addresses outside the U.S. and Canada.

faqs.question: Does Epson have a program where I can donate my working electronic equipment?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Epson America, Inc. and
Digitunity
have joined together with the goal of helping those who are facing economic challenges or have a disability to gain access to today's technology. With your donation, you not only help the environment, but you also help change the lives of those who need these products the most.

Try the following:

Close the

window before you print.
Clear space on your hard drive or run a defragmentation utility.
Close programs that you're not using.

faqs.question: Does OS X support manual duplex printing with my product?
faqs.answer: This feature is not supported in Mac OS X. However, if your printer has a built-in automatic duplexer, auto-duplexing is supported in Mac OS X 10.6 (Snow Leopard).

faqs.question: I see a communication error when I try to print with a USB connection. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following:
Make sure the USB cable is a shielded "AB" cable not more than 10 feet long.
Note:
Do not use devices that extend the length of the cable because they can cause signal degradation.
If you're using a USB hub with your printer, connect the printer directly to your computer.
Note:
Do not connect through a USB keyboard.  The keyboard acts like a hub and can interfere with signal transmission.
Use a different port on your computer.
Make sure there is no error on the printer.

faqs.question: I replaced an ink cartridge and my product shows that the same ink cartridge is expended. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
If you have just installed a new cartridge and you still see an ink related error, the cartridge may be incorrectly installed.
Follow these steps to make sure the cartridges are correctly installed:
Make sure the printer is turned on (the green power light should be on but not flashing). Then open the printer cover.
Press the ink button.The print head moves and the green power light flashes.
Lift up the cartridge cover.
Press in the tab on the back of the cartridge, lift it out of the printer and then reinsert the cartridge into the printer.
Press the cartridge down until it clicks into place.
If you need to reinstall any other ink cartridges, repeat steps 4 through 5.
Close the cartridge cover, press it down on the top until it clicks, then close the printer cover.
Press the ink button. The printer begins charging the ink delivery system.
The green power light and red ink lights flash and the printer makes noise. Charging takes about 90 seconds. When it's finished, the green power light stops flashing and stays on. The red ink light and the light(s) above the cartridge(s) go out.
Caution:
Never turn off the printer while the green power light is flashing, unless the printer hasn't moved or made noise for more than 5 minutes.

faqs.question: The color ink cartridge is expended even though I print in black only. Why does this happen?
faqs.answer:
To keep the print head clear, the printer uses a small amount of ink from all the cartridges whenever it prints and to keep the print head primed. Even if you select
Black Only
, some color ink is still being used.

faqs.question: I installed new ink cartridges and my product seems to be doing a long cleaning cycle. Is this normal?
faqs.answer:
When an ink cartridge is installed in the printer, the printer charges the ink system. This takes about two and a half minutes. While the ink is charging the green
power light flashes. Never turn off the printer while the green
power light is flashing (unless the printer hasn't moved or made noise for more than 5 minutes). This initialization is a normal and necessary process. If the printer initialization does not stop after 5 minutes, turn off the printer and contact Epson technical support for assistance.

faqs.question: How do I replace an ink cartridge?
faqs.answer:
See

in the User's Guide.

faqs.question: How do I know when an ink cartridge needs to be replaced?
faqs.answer:
When the ink replace light is on, the printer will require you to change the cartridge. You need to replace a cartridge when it's expended or it gets too old. See
Replacing an Ink Cartridge
in the User's Guide.

faqs.question: How long should an ink cartridge remain in my product if it's not used often?
faqs.answer: When an installed ink cartridge is more than six (6) months old, you may need to replace it if you notice that your printouts don't look as good as they used to. If print quality doesn't improve after cleaning and aligning the print head, you should replace the ink cartridges.

faqs.question: How do I clean and maintain my product?
faqs.answer:
In order to keep your printer clean, it is recommended that you keep it covered when not in use.  This will prevent dust from settling inside the printer. You should not operate the printer in an excessively dusty environment.
If the printer should require cleaning, we recommend using a mild detergent and water with a soft cloth to wipe the outside of the printer. Do not clean any internal parts of the printer.
To clean the paper pick-up rollers and paper feed path, use cleaning sheets which can be purchased from the Epson Store. The cleaning sheet part number is S041150.  The cleaning sheets help correct issues related to inconsistent paper feed.

faqs.question: How do I clean the print head nozzles on my product in OS X?
faqs.answer:
Follow the steps below:
Load a few sheets of plain paper in the sheet feeder.
Select
Apple
>
System Preferences
>
Print and Fax
> your Printer, then
Open Print Queue
.
Select
Printer Setup
>
Utility
>
Open Printer Utility
, then
Nozzle Check
.
Follow the on-screen instructions to print the nozzle check pattern.
Check the nozzle check pattern that prints to see if there are gaps in the lines.
If there are no gaps, the print head is clean and you're done.
If there are gaps or the pattern is faint, click
Clean
to clean the print heads.
After the printer has finished cleaning, click
Confirmation
or
Print
and another nozzle check pattern will print. If it is without any gaps or missing lines, click on
Finish

Clean

If necessary, repeat cleaning two more times. If the situation continues after three cleaning cycles, replace the affected ink cartridge(s).

faqs.question: How should I store my product if it's not going to be used for a long time?
faqs.answer:
Epson recommends storing the product in a cool, dry environment. See your product's documentation for recommended storage temperatures.
Check the ink cartridge before placing the product in storage. If the ink cartridge is very low or expended, Epson recommends replacing it with a new ink cartridge to help prevent the print head from drying out. When taking the product out of storage, check the ink cartridge again to see if it has expired. If the cartridge is expired and you experience print quality issues, you may need to replace the expired ink cartridge to improve print quality.
Make sure to turn off the product using the power button and unplug the power cord before placing it in storage. Cover the product to protect it from dust.

faqs.question: How can I stop my product from feeding multiple pages at the same time?
faqs.answer:
If multiple pages feed, follow these steps:
Remove the paper from the sheet feeder.
Fan the edges of the sheets.
Reload them against the right side of the feeder.
If you're using multiple sheets of Matte Paper in sizes larger then letter, attach the matte sheet support to the top of the sheet feeder. See
Loading Multiple Sheets of Matte Paper
for more information.
If you're using Epson Watercolor Paper, Epson Velvet Fine Art Paper, Epson UltraSmooth Fine Art Paper, PremierArt Matte Scrapbook Photo Paper for Epson or heavy set paper, load the paper in the single sheet guide. See
Loading Special Paper in the Single Sheet Guide
for more information.
Slide the left edge guide snugly, but not too tightly, against the paper. Don't load paper above the arrow on the left edge guide and make sure it is under the tabs on the left and right edge guides.
If that doesn't help, make sure the paper you're using is not too thin or too thick. If it is very humid, the paper may have absorbed moisture and should be replaced with dry paper. If necessary, try different paper from a new package.

faqs.question: Sometimes the paper doesn't eject all the way or is wrinkled. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
See
Paper Problems
in the User's Guide.

faqs.question: My product won't feed paper. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
See
Paper Problems
in the User's Guide if paper sheets won't feed correctly, won't eject fully, eject wrinkled, or jam in the printer. Also, see
Paper Problems
if roll paper doesn't feed correctly or jams in the printer.
If the printer will not pick up paper sheets and load them into the printer, try cleaning the rollers as described below.
Caution:
Never use a hard or abrasive brush, or benzine, alcohol, or thinner for cleaning; they can damage the printer components and case.
Don't get water on the printer components and don't spray or apply lubricants or oils inside the printer.
Don't use any cleaning sheets included with special paper; they may jam inside the printer.
Clean the printer's "D" roller:
Turn off and unplug the printer.
Use a lint-free, damp cloth to gently wipe the roller identified in the image below. Do not spill liquid in the printer.
Clean the rollers inside the printer:
Turn off and unplug the printer.
Push in the bottom of the output tray. The tray opens and moves up.
Lift up the printer cover and press in the top of the CD/DVD tray guide.
Lower the CD/DVD tray guide.
Use a can of compressed air to blow air from right to left in the slot above the CD/DVD tray guide. This cleans the rollers in the printer.
CD/DVD tray guide slot

faqs.answer: No.

Type

Photo Quality Ink Jet Paper

faqs.question: How do I load roll paper?
faqs.answer:
See
Loading Roll Paper
in the User's Guide.

faqs.question: How should I handle specialty paper like fine art media?
faqs.answer:
Do the following:
Always use one sheet at a time.
Use lint-free cotton gloves when handling the media.
Never stack prints on top of each other. Use a separator sheet between prints.
Store media flat. Never store media on its side.
Store media in a cool, dry environment. Refer to the media specification sheet for proper temperature and humidity requirements.
Always follow the specific loading instructions for the media being used.
Use the proper media type setting (EMX).
Note:
Non-Epson media can be optimized using custom media settings created in Epson Media Installer.

faqs.question: Which Epson Professional papers do not have optical brighteners?
faqs.answer: Hot Press Natural, Cold Press Natural, and UltraSmooth Fine Art Paper.

faqs.question: Heavy coated or thick paper does not load correctly or loads skewed. What should I do?
faqs.answer: The paper you are using may be too heavy or glossy for the paper roller to pick up. Be sure the paper is within printer specifications.

faqs.question: My printout has incorrect margins. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
See
The margins are incorrect
in the User's Guide.

faqs.question: My product is printing blank pages. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following:
Make sure your printer is selected in the
Print
window (Windows) or in the
Page Setup
and
Print
windows (Mac OS X).
Your document may have more pages than you think. Select
Print Preview
from your application's
File
menu before printing. Then either select to print only the current page, or only those pages with text, or delete the extra pages in your document before printing.
Paper settings in the printer software may be incorrect for your paper size. Check the paper size, orientation, printable area, and layout settings to make sure they're correct for your paper size.
If these suggestions don't help, the print head nozzles may be clogged. Run the printer's
Auto Nozzle Check and Cleaning Utility
to solve the problem.

faqs.question: The quality of my printed output is unacceptable. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
This problem could be due to a software setting or the printer's condition. For more information, see
Quality Problems
.
You can also try applying a color management workflow to help you to obtain consistent and predictable color reproduction in your photos.

faqs.question: My printouts are missing color and/or black print. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
If color or black is missing, the problem could be due to a software setting (your application may have been set to print black only) or the printer's condition. See
You see wrong or missing colors
for more information.

faqs.question: My product sounds as though it is printing, but nothing prints. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
You may need to
clean the print head

faqs.question: My printout has lines running through it. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
The print head nozzles may be clogged. See
Cleaning the Print Head
in the User's Guide.

faqs.question: The image look inverted, as if viewed in a mirror. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Turn off the
Mirror Image
setting in the printer driver or the mirror setting in your program.

faqs.question: Web pages don't print the way they appear on my monitor. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
The pages may not print correctly due to the web page design. Try the following:
Check for a
Printer-friendly Version
(or similarly named) option on the web page.
Change the page setup and paper size settings, and select the preview option in your browser to check the changes before you print.

faqs.question: How do I upgrade or get a new copy of the Epson Print CD software that came with my product?
faqs.answer: You can download the Epson Print CD software from the Downloads tab for your product.

faqs.question: Why can't I find the media type in the drop-down menu after I downloaded the ICC profiles?
faqs.answer: An ICC profile is a file that describes how a particular device reproduces color. The profiles downloaded  from the Epson website do not change the quality settings in the driver (Text/Image, Photo, Best Photo, Photo RPM). The profiles are used in an application such as Photoshop to produce colors more accurately, so they stay consistent when printed.  When profiles are used properly, they serve to convert RGB values to CMYK and vice versa. The media types in the printer driver drop-down list do not change. If the media you are using is not listed, select the media type that is closest to the media you are printing on for best results. It is also recommended that you check the Paper section in the Epson support site for changes in media type names.

faqs.question: Can my product be set up to print in black by default instead of color?
faqs.answer: Yes (only available in the Mac OS X driver).

faqs.question: How do I select the print resolution in the Windows software?

Rather than selecting the print resolution in the driver, you select one of the following types of documents; then the resolution is automatically selected depending on the paper type you choose to print on:
Draft

Text

Text & Image

Photo

Best Photo

Yes. Follow the steps below for your operating system.

The following instructions are for small network users only. If you're on a large network and would like to share your printer, consult your network administrator.
To install software programs in Windows XP, it's necessary to log on with a Computer Administrator account. You cannot install software programs if you log on as a Limited account user. After you install Windows XP, the user account is set as a Computer Administrator account.
To install software programs in Windows 2000, it's necessary to log on as a user with administrative privileges (a user who belongs to the Administrators group.)
Windows XP and 2000

The images in the following section are for Windows XP.

Start

For Windows 2000, click
Start

Printers

If you want Windows XP or 2000 to automatically download printer drivers for computers that are running different versions of Windows, click
Additional Drivers
and select the environment and the operating systems for the other computers. Click
OK

Click
OK

Close

Next, add the printer to each computer that will access it through the network.
Note:

For Windows 2000, click

Next

Network printer

Next

Next

Click
Next

Note:
Depending on the operating system and the configuration of the computer to which the printer is connected, the Add Printer Wizard may prompt you to install the printer driver from the printer software CD-ROM. In this case, click the
Have Disk
button and follow the on-screen instructions.
To monitor the status of a shared printer, EPSON Status Monitor 3 must be installed on each computer. EPSON Status Monitor 3 is automatically installed when you install the printer software for the first time.
Mac OS X
Use the Printer Sharing setting, which is a standard feature for Mac OS X 10.2 or later. This feature is not available with Mac OS X 10.1. See your operating system's documentation for details.

faqs.question: What is the gloss optimizer cartridge for?

faqs.question: The green  power light is on, but nothing prints. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
The problem could be due to the cabling, software settings, or the printer's condition. See
Printer Problems
in the User's Guide for more information.

faqs.question: How should I transport my product?
faqs.answer:
See
Transporting the Printer
in the User's Guide.

faqs.question: Does Epson have a program where I can donate my working electronic equipment?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Epson America, Inc. and
Digitunity
have joined together with the goal of helping those who are facing economic challenges or have a disability to gain access to today's technology. With your donation, you not only help the environment, but you also help change the lives of those who need these products the most.
